utPLSQL Test Runner

Run and debug utPLSQL (Oracle PL/SQL) unit tests against any Oracle database, right in VS Code — native Test Explorer, visual test coverage, a PL/SQL debugger and Oracle-direct execution via node-oracledb.

Why use it

  • Native Test Explorer

    Suites and tests appear in the testing view; run by test, suite, file or folder.

  • CodeLens & shortcuts

    Run and Run-with-Coverage buttons over %suite/%test, plus a Ctrl+Shift+U shortcut family.

  • Visual coverage

    Colored gutters per line and per-file statement/view coverage in the Coverage tab.

  • PL/SQL debugger

    Breakpoints and step debugging of utPLSQL tests via DBMS_DEBUG (native Debug Adapter).

  • Oracle-direct execution

    Real-time streaming through node-oracledb — no waiting for the batch to finish.

  • Schema-aware tree

    Organize tests by Schema > Package > Suite > Test, with lazy loading for large schemas.

  • Connection profiles

    Switch between DEV/TEST/PROD environments; passwords stay in SecretStorage.

  • 24 UI languages

    Follows the VS Code display language, from pt-BR to 中文 and more.

Get started

  1. Install the extension from the VS Code Marketplace.
  2. Have an Oracle database with the utPLSQL framework (UT3) installed.
  3. Configure a connection and open a .pks suite — tests show up in the Test Explorer.

FAQ

What is utPLSQL Test Runner?

A VS Code extension that runs, debugs and covers utPLSQL (Oracle PL/SQL) unit tests against an Oracle database. Suites and tests appear in the native Test Explorer, with visual test coverage and a PL/SQL debugger.

Which VS Code and Oracle versions are supported?

VS Code 1.101+ and Oracle Database 12.2+. The thin driver (node-oracledb) works out of the box; optional thick mode (Oracle Instant Client) covers environments that require Native Network Encryption.

Do I need the utPLSQL framework installed in the database?

Yes. Install the utPLSQL framework (UT3) in the Oracle database — per-schema or shared install — and grant the privileges the extension validates during setup.

Does it provide test coverage?

Yes. Statement and view coverage with colored gutters per line and per-file percentages in the Coverage tab. Coverage requires GRANT EXECUTE ON DBMS_PROFILER.

Can I debug PL/SQL tests?

Yes. Set breakpoints and step through utPLSQL tests with the native PL/SQL debugger (DBMS_DEBUG). Requires DEBUG CONNECT SESSION and EXECUTE ON SYS.DBMS_DEBUG.
